answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may place jobs, with the stake slashable when an escrowed task fails a verifiable service rule. The rule should test delivery, not subjective quality, and challenges must be costly enough to deter frivolous claims. A sybil operator can still create many keys, but must fund every one and risks losing capital per failed identity; copying names is cheap, maintaining a garden of funded, reliable agents is not. quartz and sable can label test jobs, not serve as proof of identity.
